title: Catch-all order search with a hidden ISNULL filter
prompt: Back-office search screen: about 40 calls per second at peak. About 70% of calls pass only @CustomerID, 15% pass
@LastName, and 10% pass @Status with a date range. Duration is bimodal: 2 ms to 25 s, depending on which cached
plan is in memory. Query Store shows 6 plans in the last week, and the current one scans PK_Orders. Measured
compile time for this statement is about 12 ms of CPU. The product owner says the screen works correctly today
and must keep returning the same rows.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).
baseline_sql: JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
AND (@LastName IS NULL OR c.LastName LIKE @LastName + N'%')
ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC, o.OrderID DESC;

correct_families.description: Build only the predicates that are supplied and run the text with sp_executesql and real parameters. Keep the rule that orders without a promo code are never returned.
reference_sql: JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
IF @CustomerID IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND o.CustomerID = @CustomerID';
IF @Status     IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND o.Status = @Status';
IF @FromDate   IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND o.OrderDate >= @FromDate';
IF @ToDate     IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND o.OrderDate < @ToDate';
IF @PromoCode  IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND o.PromoCode = @PromoCode'
ELSE SET @sql += N' AND o.PromoCode IS NOT NULL';
IF @MinTotal   IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND o.TotalAmount >= @MinTotal';
IF @LastName   IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND c.LastName LIKE @LastName + N''%''';
ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC, o.OrderID DESC;';
N'@CustomerID int, @Status varchar(12), @FromDate datetime2(3), @ToDate datetime2(3), @PromoCode varchar(20), @MinTotal decimal(19,4), @LastName nvarchar(80)',

traps.why: o.PromoCode = ISNULL(@PromoCode, o.PromoCode) is not an optional filter. With @PromoCode NULL it is o.PromoCode = o.PromoCode, which is never true for a NULL promo code. Leaving the predicate out returns the 85% of orders that have no promo code.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case customer_only: every order of the customer without a promo code appears.

min_improvement.basis: The cached plan scans PK_Orders. The dominant @CustomerID path must become an ordered seek that stops at 200 rows.

key.reference_notes: Tell the owner that the screen never returns orders without a promo code. That is probably a bug, but removing it is a behaviour change that needs sign-off. The static tier accepts only the dynamic SQL shape; separate procedures per search pattern are judged by the live tier.
